infra/scripts/cleanup_comment_echo_jira.py:276: "if _POSIX_MODE_BITS and stat.S_IMODE(mode) & 0o077:". On Windows nothing now checks who can write to the artifact directory, and docs/comment-echo-reclaim-runbook.md (added text) says "nothing checks for extra entries such as Users or Everyone".
Absence: after os.open there is no comparison of os.fstat(descriptor) with os.lstat(path) (st_ino/st_dev or st_file_attributes/reparse tag) to confirm the opened object is the one checked.
dropped.finding: On Windows, the new path.is_symlink() checks in _read_regular, _write_new and _append_record leave a check-then-open race that nothing after the open closes. O_NOFOLLOW is absent there (getattr returns 0), so os.open follows a symlink planted after is_symlink() returns False. The fstat S_ISREG check that follows only looks at the link's target, so a link to a regular file passes. This same change also skips the directory access check on Windows, so nothing ensures the artifact directory is free of other writers who could win that race.
scenarios: Windows operator: the artifact directory sits under a parent whose inherited ACL gives Users write access. A local user with symlink rights (Developer Mode or SeCreateSymbolicLinkPrivilege) replaces jira-before.json or the journal with a symlink between the is_symlink() check and os.open. _read_regular / _verify_existing then read attacker-chosen content, or _append_record appends Jira cleanup records to a file outside the artifact directory.
dropped.suggested_fix: After opening, run `fst = os.fstat(fd); lst = os.lstat(path)` and raise CleanupError (closing fd) unless `stat.S_ISREG(lst.st_mode)` and `(fst.st_dev, fst.st_ino) == (lst.st_dev, lst.st_ino)`. On Windows, also reject `lst.st_file_attributes & stat.FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT`.
